page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: Photoperiod is the number of light hours
Photoperiodism is the response shown by an
steps.why: Photoperiodism is named after the photoperiod, so defining the photoperiod first makes the second sentence a single short line instead of a long one.
common_mistakes: Defining photoperiodism as the length of the day. That is the photoperiod; photoperiodism is the RESPONSE to it.
Writing about light intensity. The photoperiod is about the DURATION of light.
steps.memory_tip: Photoperiod is the day length; photoperiodism is what the animal does about it.
steps.margin_note: Two short sentences: the photoperiod first, then the response to it.

steps.label: Example

lines.text: Photoperiodism: the response to day length

lines: In winter the days are short in Siberia, so
the birds move southward to a place with a
longer day for feeding and breeding.
steps.why: The example has to show a response that follows the day length and not the temperature, so the sentence must say why the birds move — the short day, not the cold.
common_mistakes: Saying the birds migrate because of the cold. In this answer the trigger is the SHORT DAY.
Giving no example at all. One of the two marks is the example.
steps.memory_tip: Short days push the birds towards the longer day: photoperiodism moves them, not the cold.
steps.margin_note: Name the example and give the reason in one line. Three lines are enough.

insider_note: The mark for the example is lost when a student writes that the birds migrate because of the cold — the answer must tie the migration to the day length.
